en_alt: Pay attention to this detail.
note: «обратить внимание» is the fixed collocation 'pay attention'; the literal en_gb stays, the idiomatic reading is added for the word-bank drill.

ru: Я обращу́ ваш взгляд на гла́вное за́втра.
en_alt: I will turn your gaze to the main thing tomorrow.
note: взгляд is rendered 'gaze' in the sibling sentence, so the literal reading is worth accepting alongside 'attention'.

ru: Ты бы обрати́л на э́то внима́ние.
en: You would have paid attention to this.
note: Perfective бы+past is a single completed event, so 'would have paid' keeps it distinct from the imperfective обращать's 'would pay'.

en_alt: Will you pay attention to the board?
note: Equally valid rendering of the обратить внимание collocation.

en_alt: I will pay attention to the mistakes.
note: Equally valid rendering of the обратить внимание collocation.

en_alt: They will go to the police.
note: 'go to the police' is the ordinary English for обратиться в полицию; en_gb stays literal.

en_alt: Will you see a doctor?
note: обратиться к врачу is normally 'see/consult a doctor'; the literal en_gb is kept.

en_alt: He sought help.
note: The Russian names no addressee, so 'to others' is invented.

en: I would turn to a specialist.
en_alt: I would consult a specialist.
note: 'address a specialist' is not idiomatic English for обратиться к; the sibling sentences all use 'turn to'.

ru: Мы бу́дем обраща́ть внима́ние на дета́ли.
en_alt: We will pay attention to the details.
We will be paying attention to the details.
note: Article and progressive variants of the imperfective compound future are equally valid.

en_alt: Are you paying attention to the noise?
note: Both the simple and progressive present render the imperfective here.

ru: Я не обраща́ла бы внима́ния на спле́тни.
Я не обраща́ю внима́ния на шум.
en_alt: I do not pay attention to the noise.
note: Equivalent negation word order; helps the word-bank drill.

ru: Ты бы обраща́лась с ним мя́гче.
note: The English is right, but обращаться с кем-л. = 'to treat', a sense the headword gloss 'to address' does not cover — the gloss may be the half that needs widening.

ru: Я обраща́юсь к вам с про́сьбой.
en_alt: I am addressing you with a request.
note: Matches the headword gloss; both renderings are natural.

ru: Тепе́рь я бу́ду обраща́ться к вам по и́мени.
en_alt: Now I will address you by name.
note: по имени is just 'by name'; the possessive in en_gb is an addition, so accept the literal reading too.

en_alt: Let's discuss this issue tomorrow.
note: вопрос is 'question' or 'issue' here; both are valid.
Perfective past 'discussed' is right; the imperfective partner is the side being sharpened to 'were discussing'.
Perfective future 'will discuss' is correct; the imperfective partner's compound future is the side moved to 'will be discussing'.

ru: На собра́нии со́трудники бу́дут обсужда́ть бюдже́т.
en: At the meeting, the employees will be discussing the budget.
note: Imperfective бу́дут+infinitive reads as ongoing 'will be discussing', which also clears the frame collision with the perfective 'Will you discuss this question tomorrow?'.

en: They were discussing the plans for a long time.
note: Durative до́лго + imperfective past is the progressive in English, and it leaves plain 'discussed' to the perfective partner.

ru: Я не обсужда́ла бы э́то при де́тях.

en_alt: Do you discuss the news?
note: Russian present imperfective covers both the simple and progressive English.

en_alt: Do you discuss the plans?
note: Russian present imperfective covers both the simple and progressive English.

en_alt: We spoke on the phone for a long time.
note: Alternative word order equally renders до́лго.

en_alt: Talk with friends every day.
note: The Russian has no possessive, so the article-free reading should also be accepted.

ru: С кем вы обща́етесь на рабо́те?
en_alt: Who do you talk to at work?
note: Colloquial equivalent of the same question.
Perfective future is right; the imperfective partner's compound future is the side being changed.

en_alt: She explained the reason for the delay.
note: опоздание is 'the delay' as readily as 'being late'.

en: You would have explained everything in detail.
note: Perfective бы+past reads as a completed event, which clears the 'would explain' collision with объяснять's «Я объясня́ла бы ме́дленнее…».

ru: Ты бу́дешь объясня́ть пра́вило шаг за ша́гом.
en: You will be explaining the rule step by step.
note: Imperfective бу́дешь+infinitive is the ongoing future; this one change clears three 'will explain' collisions with объяснить.

en_alt: Are you explaining the task to the students?
note: Both English presents render the imperfective.

ru: Я объясня́ла бы ме́дленнее на твоём ме́сте.
note: The imperfective correctly keeps the present counterfactual 'would explain'.

ru: Я огляде́л бы весь дом снача́ла.

en_alt: I am looking around me.
note: по сторонам is 'from side to side / around'; both readings are natural.
'keep looking around' carries the imperfective compound future well.

ru: Я не огля́дывалась бы так не́рвно.

en_alt: Will you look back in farewell?
note: на прощание is literally 'in farewell'; the en_gb paraphrase stays.

en_alt: I will look back in farewell.
note: на прощание is literally 'in farewell'; the en_gb paraphrase stays.
No aspect partner competes for 'would look back', so the present counterfactual reading stands.

en_alt: Look round, someone is coming.
note: British 'look round' is the everyday rendering of огляни́сь.

ru: Я одева́юсь ка́ждое у́тро за де́сять мину́т.
Я одева́лась бы ти́ше, что́бы не разбуди́ть всех.
Де́ти бы́стро оде́лись и пошли́ в шко́лу.
Она́ оде́лась и вы́шла из до́ма.
Е́сли бы не опа́здывал, я оде́лся бы.
note: The perfective conditional is already correctly rendered as 'would have got dressed'.

ru: Я ожида́ла бы бо́льшего от него́.

en_alt: I am awaiting an answer to the letter.
note: отве́т is glossed 'answer' corpus-wide; accept it alongside 'reply'.

ru: Отны́не я бу́ду ожида́ть твоего́ отве́та.
note: The imperfective compound future is already 'will be awaiting'.

en: We will find ourselves at home by evening.
en_alt: We will end up at home by evening.
note: 'find ourselves home' is not English; 'at home' is required after the reflexive.

ru: Без ка́рты я бы оказа́лся в тупике́.
Ско́ро всё ока́жется на свои́х места́х.
en: Soon everything will end up in its place.
en_alt: Soon everything will fall into place.
note: 'will turn out to be in its place' is clumsy for оказаться на своих местах, and 'end up' clears the 'will turn' collision with ока́зываться.

en: The plans kept turning out to be too complicated.
note: 'turn out' needs 'to be' before an adjective, as the sibling sentences all have it.
With the perfective partner moved to 'end up', this side keeps 'will turn out' unambiguously.

ru: Без подска́зок он ре́дко ока́зывался бы прав.

note: окончить университет is idiomatically 'graduate from university'.

ru: Она́ око́нчила шко́лу с золото́й меда́лью.

en: Are you wary of the dark?
en_alt: Are you afraid of the dark?
note: 'afraid' is боя́ться; опаса́ться is the guarded 'be wary of', as the five sibling sentences render it.

en: You would have determined the deadline precisely.
note: Perfective бы+past is a completed act, and this clears the 'would determine' collision with определя́ть's «Я определя́л бы це́ну по ка́честву.».
Frame-only collision with the stative imperfective «Пра́вила определя́ли…»; the two sentences differ in every content word, so the drill still has a cue.
Perfective future is correct; the imperfective partner's compound future is the side being sharpened.
A stative imperfective past; plain 'determined' is the right English here.

en: Experience will be determining your choice.
note: The bare 'will determine' collides with four определи́ть futures; the imperfective compound future is the ongoing 'will be determining'.

ru: Я определя́л бы це́ну по ка́честву.
note: The imperfective keeps the present counterfactual 'would determine' once the perfective partner moves to 'would have determined'.

en_alt: I determine the direction from the map.
note: по ка́рте reads as 'from the map' as naturally as 'by the map'.

en_alt: The fog will descend on the city.
note: Both the bare and definite noun phrase are natural for the Russian.

en_alt: He is yelling loud enough for the whole house to hear.
note: Spells out на весь дом more explicitly; en_gb stays as the shorter reading.

ru: Я не бу́ду ора́ть на тебя́.
note: A negated compound future is naturally 'will not yell'; the progressive would be worse English.

ru: Я не ора́л бы так гро́мко.

en_alt: We are organising a big party.
note: пра́здник covers 'celebration' and 'party' alike.

en_alt: Soon the lamps will illuminate the street.
note: Matches the headword gloss; both renderings are natural.

en_alt: I will illuminate the road with a torch.
note: доро́га is glossed 'road' corpus-wide; accept it alongside 'path'.

en_alt: Will you illuminate the room?
note: Matches the headword gloss; both renderings are natural.
